To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the highly conserved Thr132 is essential for the catalytic mechanism of wheat nucleotide pyrophosphate/phosphodiesteras

the catalytic activity of wheat NPP (TaNPPr) depends on the presence of a conserved Thr residue in the active site and on the conservation of several other amino acid residues, which are important for substrate specificity and/or activity.
six amino acid residues, which are conserved over Nucleotide Pyrophosphatases/Phosphodiesterases of different organisms, play a role in the catalytic activity of wheat NPP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the role of six conserved residues in the catalytic site and their influence on enzyme activity.
the identification of the substrate-specifying amino acid residues of NPPs and the elucidation of their catalytic mechanism.
the identification of substrate-specific amino acids of TaNPPr.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amino acids Thr132, His255, Asn153, Phe194, Asn165, and Glu199 are essential for the catalytic activity of TaNPPr.
these residues are essential for the catalytic mechanism of NPP.
the catalytic site in TaNPPr and probably all NPPs is very strict in its structural requirements, but that the catalytic mechanism is more flexible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the catalytic site residues of TaNPPr are highly conserved, whereas the substrate-binding site is more flexible.
a highly conserved Thr132 is essential, while a highly conserved histidine can be exchanged for an alanine.
only a limited number of amino acid residues can be changed without abolishing enzyme activity, and these amino acids can be found at the catalytic site.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the catalytic site is highly conserved and that only very minor changes are tolerated.
NPPs of plants and animals are very similar in their catalytic mechanisms.
the catalytic residues of the TaNPPr are very similar to those of other NPPs, and that the substrate-specific residues are less conserved.
